description_en: This two-tiered Gaṇeśa temple is located in the Navālī Ṭola of Deopatan. Topped with a gilded finial, the temple boasts simple struts. Above the entrance to the sanctum, an ornamental arch (toraṇa) with a standing figure of Gaṇeśa serves as a prominent feature. Within the sanctum, the main deity is a stone statue of a four-armed Gaṇeśa in a princely seated pose (rājalīlāsana)with a metal covering. Additionally, a statue of Viṣṇu adorns the eastern wall of the sanctum.Unfortunately, due to the lack of historical sources, the exact year of the temple's construction remains uncertain. The earliest documented record pertaining to the temple is an inscription from 1827 CE (NS 947), which chronicles the expansion of the temple during the reign of King Rājendra Vikrama Śāha. The residents of Navālī Ṭola, including Lachinārā, Āsānārā, and Dhamanārā, dismantled the previous smaller temple of Gaṇeśa and constructed a larger one. Details regarding the size and structure of the original temple are not specified in the inscription. The temple was expanded in 1827 CE (NS 947) and in 2000 CE (VS 2057), the Pashupati Area Development Trust undertook renovation efforts for the temple.As the revered Sthānagaṇeśa of Navālī Ṭola, local residents visit the temple before engaging in significant rituals and life events. No specific priest is assigned to the temple; instead, a woman from the Maharjana caste acts as the caretaker (dyaḥpāḥlāḥ) and performs daily rituals while ensuring the temple's cleanliness. The temple's anniversary ritual takes place in the solar month of Caitra. Previously, every Tuesday, a metal statue would be placed as a covering for the stone statue, a practice that ceased after the earthquakes in 2015. The metal statue was donated by Saṃyacā Saṃgata, a local resident.Notably, a large round stone ball, known locally as Bhīmasenako Guccā (marble of Bhīmasena), can be found southwest of the temple. It is believed that anyone capable of lifting the stone ball will be blessed with a son.
description_ne: नवाली टोलको स्थान गणेशको रूपमा पुजिने यो मन्दिर नेसं ९४७ (सन् १८२७) मा भत्काएर ठूलो बनाइएको थियो ।पाशुपतक्षेत्रअन्तर्गत देवपत्तन (ग्वल ) को नवाली टोलमा यो गणेश मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । देवपत्तनका नौवटा टोलमध्ये एउटा नवाली टोल हो । यी गणेश नवाली टोलका स्थानगणेश हुन् । दक्षिणाभिमुख गरी बनाइएको यस मन्दिरमा दुई तह तामाका छाना राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको गजूर राखिएको छ । मन्दिरका छानामुनि सादा टुँडालहरू राखिएका छन् । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि उभिएका गणेश अङ्कित धातुको तोरण राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र राजलीलासनमा बसेका, चार हात भएका ढुङ्गाको गणेश स्थापना गरिएको छ । ढुङ्गाको मूर्तिलाई धातुको पाताले मोडिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पूर्वी भित्तामा विष्णुको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । मन्दिरबाहिर दक्षिण-पश्चिममा भीमसेनको गुच्चा भनिने गोलो ढुङ्गा राखिएको छ । उक्त ढुङ्गा उचाल्न सक्नेले छोरा पाउँछ भन्ने विश्वास रहेको छ ।यो मन्दिरको स्थापनाबारे जानकारी दिने कुनै ऐतिहासिक सामग्री पाइएको छैन । मन्दिरमा प्राप्त सबैभन्दा पुरानो अभिलेख नेसं ९४७ (सन् १८२७) को शिलालेख हो । उक्त शिलालेखमा राजा राजेन्द्रविक्रम शाहको राज्यकालमा नवाली टोलका प्रमुख लछिनारा (लक्ष्मीनारायण) को नेतृत्वमा आसानारा, धमनारा लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर पहिलेको सानो मन्दिर भत्काएर त्योभन्दा ठूलो मन्दिर निर्माण गरेको कुरा लेखिएको छ । पुरानो मन्दिर कति तलाको थियो र पुनर्निर्माणपछि कति तलाको बनाइएको थियो भन्ने कुरा अभिलेखमा उल्लेख गरिएको छैन । विसं २०५७ (सन् २०००) मा पशुपति क्षेत्र विकास कोषबाट मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो ।यो नवाली टोलको स्थान गणेश हुनाले टोलमा कसैको जन्मदिन, पास्नी, व्रतबन्ध, भीमरथारोहण जस्ता संस्कार गर्दा सबैभन्दा पहिले यहीँ आएर पूजा गर्नुपर्ने परम्परा रहिआएको छ । मन्दिरमा कुनै पुजारी नियुक्त गरिएको छैन । महर्जन थरकी महिलाले मन्दिरको द्य:पा:ला:को रूपमा काम गरिरहेकी छिन् । उनैले मन्दिरको नित्यपूरा र सरसफाइको काम गरिरहेकी छिन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र महिनामा गणेशको वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गरिन्छ । त्यस दिन पूरै मन्दिरको सरसफाइ गरी क्षमापूजा गरिन्छ । प्रत्येक हप्ताको मंगलवार गर्भगृह भित्र रहेको गणेश मूर्तिअगाडि अर्को एउटा धातुको गणेश मूर्ति प्रदर्शन गरिन्थ्यो । मंगलवार प्रदर्शन गरिने उक्त मूर्ति स्थानीय संयचा संगत बनाउन लगाएका थिए । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पपछि उक्त प्रचलन बन्द भएको थियो ।

historical_events.event_name: Demolishing the old small temple and building a new big temple
historical_events.event_description: Under the rule of King Rājendra Vikrama Śāha, the residents of Navālī ṭola, such as Lachinārā, Āsānārā, and Dhamanārā, replaced the existing smaller Gaṇeśa temple with a larger one. Unfortunately, the inscription does not provide details about the size and structure of the old temple.
The temple was renovated by the Pashupati Area Development Trust.

Najaramāna, Cinī, Sūryamāna, and their family members installeddalūlampstands around the temple as a gesture to honor and remember their deceased family members, with the intention of wishing for their eternal peace.
Maṃgalalāla Saṃgata and his family members offered an oblong narrow banner (patāḥ) .
Gopālamāna Śreṣṭha offered an oblong narrow banner (patāḥ) at the temple.
In memory of the deceased Sājana Saṃgata, his grandfather Gopāla Saṃgata, father Surendra Saṃgata, mother Gitā, and other family members established adharmadhātujinālayacaityain front of the temple.
Śyāmakṛṣṇa Maharjana offered a bell at the temple in the name of his deceased mother Bhuyu Maharjana, who passed away in 1983 CE.
On the occasion of the birthday of Rāmaśaraṇa Maharjana, his father Rāmeśvara Maharjana offered an ornamented arch (toraṇa) of metal on top of the entrance to the sanctum.

Saṃyacā Saṃgata, son of Indramāna and Harimāyā Saṃgata, offered a pair of brass flags installed on either side of the main deity. He also offered a metaltoraṇaon top of the Gaṇeśa statue and established a pair of lions flanking the statue. Likewise, he offered a metal statue to be placed as a cover for the stone statue.
Rekhā Śreṣṭha (Vaidya) set ceramic tiles on the walls inside the sanctum in memory of her deceased father Tārānanda Vaidya.
